netWorth.title: What you’re worth
netWorth.body: What you’re worth is everything you own minus everything you owe. Right now that is {assets} in accounts and holdings, minus {liabilities} you still owe: {netWorth}. Paying off a loan does not change it — the debt and your cash both fall by the same amount.

onPaperGain.title: On-paper gain
onPaperGain.body: {direction, select, up {This gain} down {This loss} other {This figure}} is on paper: nothing has been sold, so no money has arrived. You paid {costBasis} for {quantity}; today it is worth {marketValue}, {direction, select, up {which is {delta} more} down {which is {delta} less} other {exactly what you paid}}. If the price moves tomorrow, so does this number — only selling makes it real.

fxChange.title: Change from exchange rates
fxChange.body: This change comes from the exchange rate, not from anything you spent or earned. Your {balance} was worth {valueThen} when recorded and is worth {valueNow} at today’s rate. The {balance} itself has not moved — only what it is worth in {reportingCurrency} has.

transaction.title: A transaction
transaction.body: A transaction is money moving from one place to another; nothing appears or disappears. This one moved {amount} out of {from} and into {to}. {toKind, select, expense {{to} going up is not money you have — it is the running total of what has gone there.} income {{to} is where money comes from; the same amount landed in {from}, which is yours.} liability {This paid down a debt: what you owe under {to} fell by exactly that amount.} asset {The money is still yours — it changed where it sits, not how much you have.} other {Both sides record the same amount, so the two places always agree.}}

effects.label: Reduce visual effects
effects.description: Flattens shadows and stops motion. Colour, spacing and type stay as they are.
effects.systemReduced: Your system already asks for less motion, so motion is off either way.

density.label: Dense rows
density.description: Tighter rows on larger screens. Type size never changes.
